title: 2026-03-25 Acme Healthcare POC scoping - quality eval plan
topics: quality evaluation: golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination checks, scoring
summary: AE + SE scoping call to agree on quality evaluation plan for a 6-week POC. Discussed golden prompt set, regression test suite, hallucination and format checks, scoring rubric, workload sizing for benchmarking (concurrent users, tokens/day), and timeline for deliverables. Next steps agreed: Redwood to share eval spreadsheet and sample runner, Acme to provide 1k golden prompts + priority failure cases, schedule benchmark week.
next_steps: Redwood: send quality eval spreadsheet and sample benchmark runner (Miguel) by 2026-03-27
Customer: share initial set of 1,000 golden prompts and 200 known failure/regression cases by 2026-04-01
Schedule benchmark week: target 2026-04-06 to 2026-04-10 for throughput and quality run
Meet to review results and pass/fail scoring on 2026-04-14

transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-03-25 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Miguel Santos (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Redwood CSM); Dr. Priya Sharma (Acme Head of Data), Marco Diaz (Acme ML Eng), Samantha Lee (Acme PM), Raj Patel (Acme Security)

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick intros, then we'll dive into the quality eval plan for the POC.
[00:12] Dr. Priya Sharma: Hi all, Priya here. We're primarily focused on triage and summarization flows, plus a few clinical QA checks. We're running with a mix of internal notes and patient-facing templates.
[00:25] Marco Diaz: yeah, hi, Marco. we'll also look at structured output format, JSON-ish responses that feed into our downstream EHR integration.
[00:38] Miguel Santos: great. one thing we'll aim to do today is align on success criteria and the eval artifacts — golden prompts, regression test cases, hallucination checks, and a scoring approach that matches your risk thresholds.
[00:52] Samantha Lee: timeline wise we want a quick pilot, like 4-6 weeks, must show no regressions on priority flows and <1% high-severity hallucinations for patient-facing text.
[01:10] Lena Park: noted. can you give us rough workload sizing? concurrency, tokens per request, daily volume?
[01:20] Marco Diaz: baseline is around 15 concurrent users during peak, average prompt + context ~1.2k tokens, about 250k tokens/day steady, spikes up to 800k tokens/day for batch processing.
[01:35] Miguel Santos: ok that maps to small dedicated pool or hosted with burst — we can recommend configs. For benchmarking we typically run a 'benchmark week' replicating peak load and run the quality eval against the same dataset at lower and peak throughput.
[01:50] Dr. Priya Sharma: on golden prompts — we have about 1k examples we trust, plus about 200 flagged failure cases (incorrect code mapping, wrong patient medication data, and bad JSON formatting). we'll share those.
[02:05] Miguel Santos: perfect. for the golden set we recommend labeling severity per example (critical, major, minor) so scoring weights reflect business impact. even if labels are rough it's super helpful.
[02:20] Marco Diaz: how do you do hallucination checks? automated or human review?
[02:25] Miguel Santos: combination. automated heuristics for factuality (e.g., cross-checks against patient record fields) plus human spot-checks. for clinical hallucinations we add pattern checks: unexpected entities, dates that don't match, or invented medication names. also format checks: JSON schema validation and strict parseability.
[02:45] Samantha Lee: and regression tests? we need to ensure new model/quantization doesn't break structured outputs.
[02:50] Miguel Santos: we recommend a regression suite that includes: 1) golden prompts to assert exact match or fuzzy match thresholds, 2) negative tests (should not hallucinate), 3) format tests (schema pass/fail), and 4) performance smoke (latency p95 not to exceed SLO under given concurrency).
[03:10] Lena Park: scoring approach — we generally produce a per-example composite score combining correctness, hallucination flag, format pass, and latency penalty. weights are configurable. for your use case we might weight hallucination and format higher.
[03:26] Dr. Priya Sharma: can you show an example rubric?
[03:30] Miguel Santos: sure, example: correctness 40%, hallucination penalty 30% (binary heavy penalty if critical), format/schema 20% (pass=1 fail=0, with partial credit for recoverable issues), latency 10% (p95 threshold). final pass if composite >= 0.85 for critical flows. we can tune thresholds per flow.
[03:55] Marco Diaz: what about tokenization differences and quantization artifacts — sometimes quantized models change output wording which can fail exact-match tests.
[04:05] Miguel Santos: yep, that's why we include fuzzy matching and tolerance bands. we also run paired regression: baseline model outputs vs candidate model outputs, compute similarity (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding sim), and flag high-delta cases for human review.
[04:25] Samantha Lee: what's your recommended runner for automated checks? we prefer something we can run in our CI.
[04:30] Miguel Santos: we'll share a sample benchmark runner (python scripts + a small harness) that executes the golden prompts, runs schema validation, computes scores, and emits CSVs. it's lightweight and suitable for CI. Miguel will drop that by Friday.
[04:45] Raj Patel: security question: for PII we need to know data flow — do you offer private deployment or VPC? and encrypted at rest with KMS?
[04:55] Lena Park: yes, Redwood Private supports VPC and customer-managed KMS/HSM. for the POC we can either use hosted with strict retention settings (no logs retained) or a Private trial. we'll include SOC2 docs and data flow diagrams in the packet.
[05:10] Raj Patel: also need audit logs and RBAC — can we get sample configs?
[05:15] Aisha Khan: we'll attach our RBAC and audit examples; Lena will include security docs in the follow-up.
[05:25] Dr. Priya Sharma: back to eval — for hallucination scoring is 1% high-severity acceptable? we mentioned <1% earlier.
[05:32] Miguel Santos: for patient-facing, anything above 0.5% critical hallucinations is likely a blocker, but we can set progressive thresholds: block if >1% critical, warning 0.5-1%, pass <0.5%. we'll let you pick thresholds.
[05:50] Marco Diaz: for throughput benchmarks, do you run sustained load tests or burst?
[05:55] Miguel Santos: both. we do a sustained run at steady traffic (250k tokens/day equivalent) and a peak stress test to validate autoscaling/burst capacity. we'll capture p95/p99 latencies and token cost.
[06:12] Samantha Lee: what about golden prompt coverage — we have domain-specific templates and edge-cases like handwriting OCR noise.
[06:20] Miguel Santos: include those as negative tests and label them. OCR noise is a great negative test: we expect your model to either normalize or return a structured 'unreadable' flag. that'll be a format requirement.
[06:38] Dr. Priya Sharma: scoring: I'd like outputs that fail format to be automatically routed to human review instead of going to downstream EHR. can we implement an auto-fallback?
[06:48] Miguel Santos: yes, the pipeline can return status codes and Redwood routing can route those to manual queue. we can demonstrate during POC.
[06:55] Lena Park: ok, quick recap of next steps and owners: Miguel shares sample runner and README by 2026-03-27; Priya shares golden prompts + failure cases by 2026-04-01; Lena shares pricing and security pack by 2026-03-28; schedule benchmark week 2026-04-06.
[07:15] Samantha Lee: sounds good. can you also include recommended model/quantization settings?
[07:20] Miguel Santos: yes — we'll include recommended model variants, quantization profiles (4-bit/8-bit tradeoffs), and expected quality deltas. note: heavy quantization may increase hallucination risk on edge cases; we'll surface that in the eval.
[07:35] Marco Diaz: will you run a paired regression test between the baseline and candidate model under the same seed?
[07:40] Miguel Santos: we'll run deterministic prompts where possible; some generation is nondeterministic, so we use beam/temperature controls for regression comparison and embedding-similarity thresholds.
[07:55] Dr. Priya Sharma: ok thanks, and please make the scoring spreadsheet editable so we can change weights per flow.
[08:05] Miguel Santos: will do. we'll provide CSV/Google Sheet template.
[08:12] Lena Park: any final questions?
[08:15] Raj Patel: one more — data residency. can you guarantee EU data stays in eu region for EU users?
[08:22] Lena Park: yes, Redwood has region routing and can pin requests to EU-hosted infra. we'll include region and residency options in the security pack.
[08:35] Samantha Lee: thanks everyone. looking forward to the runner and the eval spreadsheet.
[08:40] Lena Park: thanks all — we'll follow up with artifacts and schedule.
[08:45] Meeting end.
notes: Transcript contains occasional transcription errors (e.g., 'K V cash' for 'KV cache', 'quantize' sometimes transcribed), and some speaker labels simplified. The team agreed on a 4-6 week pilot with a benchmark week and a clear quality rubric.
final_pass_criteria: Composite score >= 0.85 for critical flows, critical hallucination rate < 0.5%, format/schema pass rate > 99% for patient-facing outputs, latency p95 under agreed SLO during peak tests
benchmarks_planned: Golden prompts run: 1,000 examples with severity labels
Throughput tests: sustained 250k tokens/day and peak stress up to 800k tokens/day
Latency: measure p50/p95/p99 under 15 concurrent users and at peak
eval_details: Golden prompts: customer provides examples, Redwood will run and produce per-example scores
Regression tests: paired comparisons vs baseline and flag high-delta cases for human review
Hallucination checks: automated heuristics + human spot check for critical flows
Format checks: JSON schema validation with strict pass/fail and recoverable warnings
risk_and_mitigations: Quantization risk: can increase hallucinations on edge cases; mitigation: run paired evals and keep non-quantized fallback for critical flows
PII/data flow: use Private/VPC or hosted w/ no retention for POC; provide SOC2 docs and KMS options
Format regressions: fail closed routing to human review before EHR ingestion
